entities.summary:
Astorgio Agnensi (1391–1451) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, multiple papal governor and multiple Curiate official.

Agnensi was born in unknown to the world, but his influence spanned global regions and continents.

The core events of his life revolved around his ascension to the papacy, his governance of various papal territories, and his role in the Catholic Church.

His legacy includes the shaping of regional Catholic governance structures and the establishment of the Agnensi family dynasty in Italy.

His contemporaries would recall Agnensi as a key figure in the tumultuous politics of the 15th century, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Catholic Church's governance and administration.

The Agnensi family's influence continued for centuries, with his descendants rising to prominence in the Italian Renaissance.
